transcript.text: Hi, my Hotpoint Aquarius dryer is taking forever to dry and the top gets really hot. Model is TCM580GUK if that helps

A very hot top together with very slow drying most often points to restricted airflow: the dryer is making heat but cannot move it through the clothes properly. A blocked fluff filter or condenser is the first thing to rule out; a heavily loaded drum, poorly spun washing, or a low-heat programme can also make drying take much longer. With it switched off, unplugged and fully cool, remove and clean the door fluff filter, then check the condenser behind the lower front flap and rinse off any fluff if it is dirty; let it drain before refitting. If those are clear but it still gets unusually hot or starts cutting out, stop using it and arrange an engineer, as the thermostat/overheat protection or internal airflow system may need attention.

Thank you. I unplugged it and let it cool, then checked the door filter, which had a thick layer of fluff on it (I'll admit I sometimes forget to clean it). The condenser at the front bottom had lint packed on the fins, so I rinsed it and it looks much cleaner now. I should also say I often run the dryer while I'm out at work. Is that a concern given how hot the top gets?

Yes — do not run it while you are out, at least until it has been retested and is drying normally. A tumble dryer’s top can become warm in use, but unusually high heat together with very slow drying is a warning sign of restricted airflow; the thick fluff and packed condenser lint give a strong explanation for that in this case. Let the condenser drain properly, refit it securely, then do one short, supervised test only with a small well-spun load on a normal heat setting. If it still takes a long time or the top becomes exceptionally hot again, stop using it and arrange an engineer to check the internal air path, fan and overheat controls. Also check Hotpoint’s official tumble-dryer safety/recall checker using the full model and serial number before returning it to regular use, as some older Hotpoint dryers were included in safety modification programmes.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]

candidates: Restricted airflow from a clogged fluff filter, condenser or vent path (high)
Laundry load too wet, too large, or a low-heat programme (medium)
Thermostat/thermal cut-out or heater fault following overheating (low)
